name: PCR THERMAL CYCLER
desc: Premium Gradient PCR Thermal Cycler engineered for high-throughput DNA amplification and precise molecular diagnostics. Features a 96 x 0.2 ml block capacity driven by a long-service-life Peltier system with an adjustable pressure hot lid and a 5-inch large color touchscreen display.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS PCR THERMAL CYCLER employs Peltier-driven thermoelectric heating and cooling with precise PID feedback control to execute high-throughput polymerase chain reaction (PCR) for DNA amplification. The system rapidly cycles a 96-well block through user-defined denaturation (~95°C), annealing (55–65°C), and extension (72°C) temperatures, enabling exponential amplification of target nucleic acid sequences by Taq polymerase in the presence of dNTPs, MgCl₂, and sequence-specific primers. Its adjustable-pressure hot lid (up to 105°C) prevents condensation and sample evaporation, while the wide 30°C–99°C gradient function allows simultaneous annealing-temperature optimisation for primer sets. This instrument is used by doctors and clinical laboratories for molecular diagnostics of pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2, Mycobacterium tuberculosis, HIV, and hepatitis viruses; by B.Sc/M.Sc students studying genetics, microbiology, and molecular biology; and by PhD researchers and chemists quantifying gene expression via SYBR Green or TaqMan probe-based qPCR, performing genotyping, site-directed mutagenesis, and forensic STR analysis. It supports compliance with ISO 15189 medical laboratory quality requirements, ASTM E1873-04 for nucleic acid detection, and CLSI MM03 molecular diagnostic guidelines.
sop: Power on the INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS PCR Thermal Cycler using the rear power switch and allow the Android touchscreen interface to initialize.
Open the heated lid and place the sealed 96-well PCR plate or 0.2 ml tube strips containing template DNA, primers, dNTPs, MgCl₂, and Taq polymerase into the block.
Close the lid and set the heated lid temperature to 105°C to prevent sample evaporation and condensation.
Press the 'SET' button once to access the block temperature setpoint on the PID controller.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter (e.g., 95°C for initial denaturation).
Press 'SET' again to lock the value and store the selected parameter.

Program the thermal cycling protocol: initial denaturation 95°C for 3 min, then 30–35 cycles of 95°C for 30 s, 55–65°C annealing for 30 s, and 72°C extension for 30–60 s, final extension 72°C for 5 min.
Set the gradient range if optimisation across 30°C–99°C is required, using the touchscreen gradient editor.
Press 'RUN' to start the amplification; monitor real-time temperature and ramping rate (max 5°C/s) on the display.
After completion, allow the block to cool to near ambient before opening the lid. Remove the PCR plate and discard used consumables as biohazard waste.
Clean the block and lid with 70% ethanol or 10% bleach solution after use; do not autoclave the block.

SAFETY WARNING: Never open the heated lid while the block is above 50°C; the hot lid and block can cause severe burns, and sudden pressure release may cause sample boiling or contamination. Always wear thermal-resistant gloves and eye protection when handling hot plates.
